timing: One warmup, median of 3 runs per method and prefix size; 20000 points per fixture.

outcomes.exact_farthest_point: 4096 samples of 20000 in 15.6 ms (box) and 10.6 ms (surface); coverage radius is the reference (1.0): only the coupled sieve comes within 0.1% (sometimes marginally below, as greedy FPS is not optimal); every other method is at least 2.5% worse
outcomes.coupled_sieve_eta095: coverage within 0.1% of exact FPS at the same CPU time; its gain is GPU batching (METHOD-060)
outcomes.flat_and_lazy_greedy_beta110: coverage 1.03-1.08x exact FPS; 13-20x slower than the sieve on the CPU because their batches rescan all points (GPU-oriented designs, METHOD-061/062)
outcomes.progressive_poisson: whole hierarchy in 29-43 ms; coverage 1.3-1.8x FPS; nearest-neighbor CV 0.11-0.24
outcomes.sample_elimination: most even at k=4096 on the box (CV 0.070) but degrades and slows at large input/output ratios (k=256 of 20000: CV 0.74, 1.7 s), as its weight limiting prescribes
outcomes.tournament: 2.7 ms, a hierarchy baseline with 1.7-2.7x FPS coverage
outcomes.guarantees: no eta/beta bound violation on any batch (quality_error_l2 = 0)

known_artifacts: coverage_vs_fps is 0 for random because it runs before the farthest-point reference in the method loop; its absolute coverage_radius is reported.
